items.subject: MA
items.prompt: What is the value of the digit 6 in 3,604,215?
items.explanation: In 3,604,215 the 3 is in the millions place and the 6 is in the hundred thousands place, so the 6 is worth 600,000.
items.misconceptions: miscounts the places

why.A: 6,000 is two places too small. Count from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands.
why.B: 60,000 is one place too small. The 6 is in the hundred thousands place.
why.D: 6,000,000 is the millions place, where the 3 is. The 6 is one place to its right.

items.explanation: Write a 0 for every place that is not named: 2 millions, 0 hundred thousands, 4 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones: 2,040,305.
items.misconceptions: drops or misplaces zero placeholders

why.B: 2,040,350 puts the 5 in the tens place. The 5 is just 5 ones.
why.C: 2,400,305 puts the 4 in the hundred thousands place. 40,000 is 4 ten thousands.
why.D: 2,403,005 slides the 4 and the 3 one place too far left.

items.prompt: What is 7,349 rounded to the nearest hundred?
items.explanation: Look at the tens digit, 4. It is less than 5, so the 3 hundreds stay and everything after becomes 0: 7,300.
items.misconceptions: rounds to the wrong place; rounds up on a 4

why.A: 7,000 rounds to the nearest thousand, not the nearest hundred.
why.C: 7,350 rounds to the nearest ten.
why.D: 7,400 rounds up, but the tens digit is 4, which is less than 5, so round down.

items.subskill: rounding to the nearest ten thousand
items.prompt: What is 285,612 rounded to the nearest ten thousand?

items.misconceptions: rounds to the wrong place; rounds down on a 5

why.A: 280,000 rounds down, but the thousands digit is 5, so round up.
why.B: 286,000 rounds to the nearest thousand.
why.D: 300,000 rounds to the nearest hundred thousand.

items.explanation: Regroup across the zeros: 5,003 becomes 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 13 ones. Then 13 − 7 = 6, 9 − 6 = 3, 9 − 8 = 1 and 4 − 1 = 3: 3,136.

why.B: 3,236 uses 10 − 8 = 2 in the hundreds. After regrouping, the hundreds digit is 9, so 9 − 8 = 1.
why.C: 4,864 takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column (7 − 3, 6 − 0, 8 − 0). Regroup instead.
why.D: 6,870 adds the numbers.

why.A: 222 writes 2 for 25 ÷ 6, but 6 × 4 = 24 still fits in 25, so the middle digit is 4.

why.D: 8,712 multiplies 1,452 by 6.

items.subskill: what a remainder means in a story
items.prompt: A baker has 150 cookies. She packs them in boxes of 12. How many boxes can she fill completely?

items.misconceptions: rounds up when the question asks for full groups

why.B: 12.5 is the exact quotient, 150 ÷ 12, but half a box is not a full box.
why.C: 13 counts the leftover cookies as a box, but the question asks for boxes filled completely.
why.D: 138 subtracts 12 from 150.

why.D: 168 multiplies all 7 packs by 24. Only 3 of the packs hold 24.

items.explanation: Multiply first: 2 × 5 = 10. Then go left to right: 18 − 10 = 8, and 8 + 4 = 12.

why.A: 0 adds 5 + 4 first and then multiplies by 2. Add and subtract left to right, after the multiplication.
why.B: 4 takes away both 10 and 4. After 18 − 10 = 8, the + 4 is added.
why.D: 84 works left to right from the start, (18 − 2) × 5 + 4. Multiply first.

items.prompt: Which number is a factor of 84?

why.D: 10 does not divide 84: 84 ÷ 10 is 8 with 4 left over. Multiples of 10 end in 0.
why.B: 8 does not divide 84: 84 ÷ 8 is 10 with 4 left over.
why.C: 9 does not divide 84: 84 ÷ 9 is 9 with 3 left over (8 + 4 = 12, not a multiple of 9).

items.explanation: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 29 cannot be divided evenly by 2, 3 or 5, so it is prime.

why.A: 21 = 3 × 7, so it has factors besides 1 and itself.
why.C: 27 = 3 × 9, so it is not prime. Odd is not the same as prime.
why.B: 25 = 5 × 5, so it is not prime.

items.prompt: The sum of two odd numbers is always
items.explanation: Each odd number is one more than an even number, so two odd numbers have two extra ones, which make a pair. 3 + 5 = 8, 7 + 9 = 16: always even.
items.misconceptions: guesses odd + odd = odd

why.A: Try it: 3 + 5 = 8 and 7 + 9 = 16. The sum is never odd.
why.C: 3 + 5 = 8, and 8 is not prime.
why.D: A multiple of 4 is not guaranteed: 3 + 7 = 10, and 10 is not a multiple of 4.

why.C: 300 divides 6,000 by 20, but 29 is much closer to 30.

why.C: 40,909 has 9 hundreds but 0 tens; 40,990 has 9 tens.

items.subject: MA
items.prompt: Which number is fifty thousand six hundred eight?
items.explanation: Fifty thousand is 50,000, six hundred is 600, and eight is 8. 50,000 + 600 + 8 = 50,608. The tens place gets a 0.
items.misconceptions: drops or adds a zero

why.A: 5,608 is five thousand six hundred eight. Fifty thousand needs five digits before the hundreds.
why.B: 50,068 is fifty thousand sixty-eight. "Six hundred" puts the 6 in the hundreds place.
why.C: 50,600 leaves out the eight. Eight goes in the ones place.

items.explanation: Divide the top and the bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. 6/8 = 3/4.

why.A: 5/7 takes 1 away from the top and the bottom. To keep the same value, divide both by the same number.
why.C: 12/14 adds 6 to the top and the bottom. Adding changes the value; multiplying both by 2 would give 12/16.
why.D: 8/6 turns the fraction upside down. 8/6 is more than 1, and 6/8 is less than 1.

why.A: 1/2 is 0.5, and 3/5 is 0.6, so 1/2 is less.
why.C: 4/7 is about 0.57, a little less than 3/5, which is 0.6.
why.B: 5/9 is about 0.56, less than 3/5, which is 0.6.

items.prompt: There are 32 students in the band. Three-eighths of them play drums. How many play drums?

items.misconceptions: stops at one eighth; forgets to divide

why.A: 4 comes from 32 ÷ 8, just one eighth. Three-eighths is three of those groups.
why.C: 20 is the students who do not play drums (5/8 of 32).
why.D: 96 multiplies 32 by 3 without dividing by 8.

items.subject: MA
items.explanation: Each whole is 7 sevenths, so 3 wholes are 21 sevenths. Add the 2 sevenths: 21 + 2 = 23. 3 2/7 = 23/7.
items.misconceptions: multiplies the wrong pair of numbers

why.A: 6/7 multiplies 3 × 2 and keeps the 7. That is less than 1, and 3 2/7 is more than 3.
why.B: 13/7 multiplies 3 × 2 and adds 7. Multiply the whole number by the bottom number: 3 × 7 = 21, then add 2.
why.D: 32/7 writes the 3 and 2 side by side. 3 wholes are 21 sevenths, not 30.

items.subject: MA
items.prompt: Which mixed number is equal to 29/4?
items.explanation: 29 ÷ 4 = 7 with 1 left over. So 29/4 is 7 wholes and 1 fourth: 7 1/4.
items.misconceptions: gets the remainder wrong

why.A: 6 1/4 is 25/4. Four sixes are 24, which leaves 5 fourths, enough for another whole.
why.C: 7 3/4 is 31/4. 29 ÷ 4 is 7 with 1 left over, not 3.
why.D: 8 1/4 is 33/4. Eight fours are 32, which is more than 29.

items.explanation: Make sixths: 1/3 = 2/6. Then 5/6 − 2/6 = 3/6, which is 1/2.

why.B: 4/6 subtracts 1 from 5 but leaves 1/3 as it is. 1/3 is 2/6, so take away 2 sixths, not 1.
why.C: 7/6 adds the fractions (5/6 + 2/6). The question subtracts.
why.D: 4/3 subtracts the tops and the bottoms (5 − 1 over 6 − 3). Make the bottoms match first.

items.subject: MA
items.explanation: Add the wholes: 2 + 1 = 3. Add the fractions: 1/2 = 2/4, and 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4, which is 1 1/4. 3 + 1 1/4 = 4 1/4.
items.misconceptions: forgets to carry the extra whole; adds tops and bottoms

why.A: 3 1/4 adds the wholes (2 + 1 = 3) and keeps only the 1/4 left over from 5/4. The extra whole in 5/4 goes onto the 3.
why.B: 3 4/6 adds the tops and the bottoms of the fractions (1 + 3 over 2 + 4). Make fourths first: 1/2 = 2/4.
why.D: 5 1/4 counts the extra whole from 5/4 twice.

why.D: 7/8 adds the piece back on. The piece was cut off, so subtract.

why.A: 5/6 is 1/6 away from 1, the biggest gap of the four.

why.C: 9/10 is 1/10 away from 1. Twelfths are smaller pieces than tenths, so 11/12 is closer.
